record.tranche_reason: The paper proposes and evaluates a reasons-based neuron-interpretation method, but does not measure the audit shares, test the specified cross-model or Inception claims, build attribution graphs, or evaluate explanations with the tests described in V6 or V7.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemanticity and reports reason strengths and interventions on neurons or residual-stream positions. These results do not measure any claim version as stated. The LeNet and Qwen intervention results are retained as related findings; the paper's other experiments on training, fairness, and robustness do not directly test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces a reasons-vector interpretability method and validates it with interventions on LeNet neurons and Qwen2.5-0.5B residual-stream positions. It does not estimate shares of neurons with one, two or unknown jobs. It does not compare models or scales, examine InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, or build neuron attribution graphs. It also does not test whether explanations from activating examples predict firing, or score explanations by simulation. Polysemanticity is mentioned only as a motivation. The intervention results measure the faithfulness of the authors' own method, which is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors claim their forward-pass reasons method is grounded, uniform, scalable, faithful, correct, trainable and useful for robustness and fairness. They stress breadth over depth and call for bigger models and harder tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces reasons vectors based on a philosophical theory of reasons; it is not a replication of the neuron-pole audit or the automated explanation-scoring method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation across layers: reason strengths are generally stronger in later layers, and early convolutional layers show less clear label clustering than the hidden linear layer. It also reports different intervention success for different MNIST digits.

fits_no_version.finding: Intervening on reason-strength-selected components shifted predictions in the intended direction. In LeNet, pos2neg succeeded 100% for most digits and neg2pos about 60%. In Qwen2.5-0.5B residual positions, about 98% of predictions flipped.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons or residual positions selected by forward-pass reason strengths causally control the target label in small models; this says nothing about the share of neurons with a single job.

record.code_released: https://github.com/LevinHornischer/ReasonsMethod (source code said to eventually be made available)
record.problems: The paper says its experiments emphasize breadth rather than depth and calls for testing bigger models and harder tasks. The Qwen experiment uses Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, described as small by contemporary standards, and its intervention success rates are reported without uncertainty estimates in the text. The LeNet intervention outcomes are given in aggregate descriptions rather than individual digit values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Other experiment results, including reasons-training effects on robustness and fairness, were omitted because they do not directly test the listed neuron-audit, neuron-explanation, or explanation-scoring claims. Figure-only reason-strength and generation statistics were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Shares of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one, two or unknown jobs.
Audit shares across dense or mixture-of-experts models and across scale.
Re-reading of InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons (pose, recursive generalization).
Interpretable-neuron share as a function of architecture or tools.
Neuron-level attribution graphs compared with replacement models; circuits are mentioned only as future work.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict firing.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The LLM 'neurons' are residual-stream dimensions, not MLP neurons. The reasons-training robustness and fairness results are correctly left out, as they are irrelevant to the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the share of neuron poles with one, two, or unknown jobs.
Does not compare the audit shares across models, architectures, or scales.
Does not examine InceptionV1's cat-and-car example, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not compare vision-model interpretability shares across architectures or tools.
Uses neuron-associated reason vectors and tests interventions, but does not build attribution graphs or compare their explanatory account with a trained replacement model or reconstruction error.
Tests interventions using a separate sentence set, but does not test whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Does not score explanations by simulating neuron activations on new text.
